ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, below is a branch containing ammeter A and unknown resistor Rx connected in series; voltmeter V is connected through the upper branch between the two end nodes of this lower series branch, therefore the voltmeter measures the voltage across the whole of ammeter A and resistor Rx connected in series. Reasoning: It is known that the voltmeter reading is 10 V, the ammeter reading is 0.1 A, and the internal resistance of the ammeter is 0.2 Ω. Since 10 V is applied across the total series resistance of the ammeter internal resistance and Rx, the total series resistance is R_total = V / I = 10 / 0.1 = 100 Ω. This total resistance includes the ammeter internal resistance 0.2 Ω and Rx, so Rx = 100 - 0.2 = 99.8 Ω.

From the text, take V = 10 V, I = 0.1 A, and ammeter internal resistance r_A = 0.2 Ω. Treat the voltmeter reading as the voltage across the series combination, so the total resistance in that branch is 10/0.1 = 100 Ω. Since this total includes the ammeter's 0.2 Ω internal resistance plus Rx, compute Rx = 100 - 0.2 = 99.8 Ω.
